items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (ureagenesis as ammonia detoxification); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (hepatic ammonia clearance); OTC deficiency OMIM 311250 | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-141 (24.5: Protein Metabolism): 'In the urea cycle, ammonium is combined with CO2, resulting in urea and water. items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology 3rd ed., 'The Heart as a Pump' (Swan-Ganz wedge pressure).
items.mechanism: With a static column from the wedged catheter through the pulmonary capillaries to the left atrium, PCWP equilibrates with and tracks left atrial pressure.

items.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st ed., 'Pulmonary Hypertension' (echo estimation of PASP).
items.mechanism: In the absence of pulmonary valve stenosis the right ventricle and pulmonary artery are continuous in systole, so RV systolic pressure equals systolic pulmonary artery pressure; elevated PAP raises RVSP (basis of the echocardiographic TR-jet estimate of PASP from RVSP).

items.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st ed., 'Pulmonary Hypertension' / 'Cor Pulmonale'; Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology 3rd ed.
items.mechanism: Sustained elevation of pulmonary artery pressure raises right ventricular afterload; the failing/congested right ventricle transmits elevated filling pressure backward, raising right atrial (central venous) pressure.

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology 3rd ed., 'Arterial pressure' (pulse pressure ~ SV / arterial compliance). | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-112 (20.3: Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance): 'a low or narrow [pulse pressure] may occur in patients with a low stroke volume... a high or wide pulse pressure is common in healthy people following strenuous exercise, when...pulse pressure...may increase...as stroke volume increases.'
items.mechanism: Pulse pressure = systolic - diastolic arterial pressure; for a given arterial compliance, a larger ejected stroke volume per beat raises systolic pressure more than diastolic, widening pulse pressure.

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology 3rd ed., 'The Heart as a Pump' (cardiac index definition).
items.mechanism: Cardiac index is cardiac output normalized to body surface area (CI = CO / BSA); at fixed body surface area cardiac index rises with cardiac output.

items.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism
items.mechanism: 5,6-dihydrothymine is the DPYD product from thymine.

items.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism
items.mechanism: N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine (ureidopropionate) is the DPYS ring-opening product of dihydrouracil.

items.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism
items.mechanism: N-carbamoyl-beta-aminoisobutyrate (ureidoisobutyrate) is the DPYS product of dihydrothymine.

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal handling of calcium; filtered load); Rose & Post, Clinical Physiology of Acid-Base and Electrolyte Disorders (hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria)
items.mechanism: urinary calcium excretion = filtered load (plasma [Ca] x GFR) minus tubular reabsorption; raising plasma calcium raises the filtered load and thus calcium excretion (e.g. hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria)

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal phosphate handling); Brenner & Rector's The Kidney (phosphate excretion)
items.mechanism: filtered phosphate load = plasma [PO4] x GFR; higher plasma phosphate raises filtered load and urinary phosphate excretion

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal urate handling); Harrison's (uric acid excretion) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.4 (Nitrogenous Wastes): uric acid is formed from purine breakdown; excess plasma urate is excreted in urine
items.mechanism: filtered urate load = plasma [urate] x GFR; higher plasma urate raises filtered load and (net of reabsorption) urinary urate excretion

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal sodium handling; filtered load)
items.mechanism: filtered sodium load = plasma [Na] x GFR; higher filtered Na (all else equal) raises distal Na delivery and urinary sodium excretion

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal potassium secretion; plasma K as a primary driver of distal K secretion)
items.mechanism: hyperkalemia stimulates aldosterone-independent and aldosterone-dependent distal K secretion; higher plasma potassium raises renal potassium excretion

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal magnesium handling); Rose & Post (Mg excretion)
items.mechanism: filtered magnesium load = plasma [Mg] x GFR; higher plasma magnesium raises filtered load and urinary magnesium excretion (and reduces TAL paracellular reabsorption)

items.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Azotemia and Urinary Abnormalities' (creatinine as an inverse GFR marker); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (creatinine clearance ~ GFR)
items.mechanism: creatinine is produced at a near-constant rate and cleared almost entirely by glomerular filtration; at steady state plasma [creatinine] is inversely related to GFR (falling GFR raises plasma creatinine)

items.evidence: Harrison's, 'Azotemia and Urinary Abnormalities' (BUN rises with falling GFR); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal urea handling) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.4 (Nitrogenous Wastes): BUN is used as an indicator of kidney function; impaired GFR reduces urea clearance and raises BUN
items.mechanism: urea is filtered and partially reabsorbed; at steady state with constant urea production, plasma urea nitrogen rises as GFR falls (azotemia)

items.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (cystatin C as a GFR estimator); Brenner & Rector's The Kidney (cystatin C and GFR)
items.mechanism: cystatin C is produced at a constant rate by all nucleated cells, freely filtered, and catabolized by the proximal tubule; plasma cystatin C is inversely related to GFR (an endogenous GFR marker)

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (creatinine filtered and excreted; clearance ~ GFR); Harrison's (urine creatinine in clearance estimation)
items.mechanism: at steady state urinary creatinine excretion equals near-constant creatinine production; the spot urine creatinine level is filtration-driven and falls when GFR is very low (oliguric AKI), so higher GFR supports higher urine creatinine output

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (urea recycling and the countercurrent multiplier; contribution of urea to maximal urine concentration)
items.mechanism: urea recycling into the inner medulla contributes substantially to the medullary osmotic gradient that drives maximal urine concentration; higher delivered urea raises achievable urine osmolality

items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin coenzymes: methylcobalamin for methionine synthase); cblC/cblF/cblJ intracellular-cobalamin disorders reduce both coenzyme forms
items.mechanism: intracellular cobalamin (from cellular uptake) is processed to methylcobalamin (the MTR / methionine-synthase coenzyme); reduced cobalamin uptake lowers methylcobalamin

items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin coenzymes: adenosylcobalamin for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase); intracellular cobalamin-processing disorders (cblA/cblB) reduce adenosylcobalamin
items.mechanism: intracellular cobalamin (from cellular uptake) is processed in mitochondria to adenosylcobalamin (the methylmalonyl-CoA-mutase coenzyme); reduced cobalamin uptake lowers adenosylcobalamin

items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin vitamers / coenzyme forms derive from the cobalamin pool); Harrison's, 'Megaloblastic Anemias'
items.mechanism: methylcobalamin is a coenzyme form derived from the body cobalamin pool; lower total cobalamin lowers the methylcobalamin available

items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin vitamers / coenzyme forms derive from the cobalamin pool)
items.mechanism: adenosylcobalamin is a coenzyme form derived from the body cobalamin pool; lower total cobalamin lowers the adenosylcobalamin available

items.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (5-methyl-THF is the dominant plasma folate); Harrison's, 'Folate deficiency'
items.mechanism: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is the principal circulating form of folate; total blood folate and 5-methyl-THF move together (5-methyl-THF is ~the measured blood folate)

items.evidence: GeneReviews / OMIM 613068 (cerebral folate transport deficiency, FOLR1); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (choroid-plexus transport)
items.mechanism: CSF folate is actively transported from blood across the choroid plexus by the folate receptor FOLR1 (cerebral folate transport); lower blood folate lowers CSF folate (and FOLR1 LoF causes isolated CSF folate deficiency)

items.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal urate handling, URAT1/SLC22A12, GLUT9/SLC2A9); Harrison's Nephrology and Acid-Base Disorders (uric acid excretion); renal hypouricemia OMIM 220150
